segments.text: Gumgumi takes a sip of cold water.
The outside of a tooth feels evenly hard.
Under the enamel is a layer called dentin.
It has tiny tubes leading to the nerve.
Those tubes are filled with fluid.
Cold makes that fluid suddenly shift.
The nerve reads that shift as a sting.
Back in the mouth, that same spot stings.
Moving fluid inside those tubes is what makes cold water sting.
